LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights A look at where the odds and spreads currently stand heading into Week 9, including a big move in Baltimore Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens will likely have to go the rest of the 2026 regular season without star quarterback Lamar Jackson . The two-time NFL MVP made his return to action on Sunday after a three-game absence due to an ankle injury, but that comeback was very short-lived. On the first play from scrimmage for the Ravens offense, Jackson jammed his right thumb on Bills pass rusher Greg Rousseau on a follow-through. That injury not only knocked him out of the game, but head coach Jesse Minter told reporters postgame that Jackson will go on injured reserve and will undergo surgery. On top of this injury turning Baltimore's season upside down, it's also thrown the line for their Week 9 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars for a loop. Not only did Jackson go down on Sunday, but backup Tyler Huntley (toe) also did, and his status for Week 9 is up in the air. That could result in undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano getting the start. With that uncertainty under center, it's no surprise to see the Ravens go from being a 3-point favorite at home to now an 8.5-point home underdog. The total also dropped from 48.5 down to 43.5. This just shows how much a line can swing when a player of Jackson's caliber is sidelined. While we won't see as dramatic of swings throughout the rest of the Week 9 slate, there has been some notable movement that is worth pointing out. So, as we close the book on Week 8, let's take our first glimpse at the upcoming week and who the oddsmakers have coming out on top. Note : Pittsburgh and Tennessee are on the bye in Week 9. Baltimore is now an 8.5-point home underdog to the Jaguars after opening as a field goal favorite. The total also dropped down to 43.5 after opening at 48.5. Jacksonville is 4-3 ATS on the season, which includes a 1-1 ATS record on the road. Amid all of the QB turnover even prior to this latest Jackson injury, the Ravens enter Week 9 0-3 ATS at home. The NFL heads back out into international waters for this matchup between the Bengals and Falcons, this time to Madrid. Cincinnati has opened as a field goal favorite as Joe Burrow and the offense are starting to find their rhythm after the Bengals QB just totaled six touchdowns in a win over Tennessee. Meanwhile, Michael Penix Jr . imploded for the Falcons, throwing four interceptions in a loss to Tampa Bay. The Bengals are 3-4 ATS this season, while the Falcons are 3-5 ATS. The total moved up to 51.5 after opening at 49.5, and the Over is 9-6 combined between these two teams this season. Denver is coming off another comeback win, this time rallying to defeat the Chiefs at home to take over first place in the AFC North. Now, they'll look to win their fifth-straight game when they visit the Panthers. Carolina will have the rest advantage over the Broncos after playing last Thursday, but are home dogs. Denver is laying 3-points as a road favorite. The Broncos' 6-2 ATS record is tied for the best in the NFL, but the club is 2-2 ATS on the road. However, as a road favorite, Denver is 2-0 ATS. As a home underdog, the Panthers are 1-1 ATS entering Week 9. The total sits at 44.5, and the Under is a combined 9-6 between these squads. New Orleans was on the bye in Week 8, so it'll be well-rested when it squares off against the Browns on Sunday. The Saints are a 3-point favorite at home and are still looking for their first ATS victory at the Superdome (0-3 ATS). On the road this season, the Browns are 2-3 ATS. With the total sitting at 43.5, it's worth noting that the Over is 2-1 in Saints home games this season. Dallas has jumped out as a 6-point favorite after the line initially opened Cowboys -4.5. This has more to do with Indy's ongoing implosion and the possibility that it continues to sell off pieces before the deadline. On Sunday, the Colts lost 42-7 to the Jaguars and Daniel Jones was benched. It's unclear if Jones will start in Week 9. If he doesn't, Anthony Richardson would likely get the nod. Dallas is 2-2 ATS on the road, but that includes a 1-2 ATS mark as a road favorite. Indy is 1-2 ATS at Lucas Oil Stadium. The total for this game jumped up to 52.5 after opening at 51.5. The Over is 6-2 in Cowboys games this season. The Rams have quietly stabilized after a 2-4 start to the regular season. They've won two straight to get back to .500 on the year and are now a 5.5-point road favorite as they gear up for a matchup against the Commanders. LA is 4-4 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS on the road. Both of those ATS road wins came as road favorites. Meanwhile, the Commanders are 1-0 ATS as a home underdog. After handing Minnesota its first loss of the season, the Lions now head down to South Beach as a 7-point road favorite over the Dolphins. Detroit is 1-2 ATS on the road, which includes a 1-1 ATS record as a road favorite. At Hard Rock Stadium, the Dolphins are 2-1 ATS. The total sits at 48.5. Between these two teams this season, the Over is 9-5. Kansas City is now a double-digit favorite over the Jets, laying 10 points after the line opened at 9.5. The Chiefs fell out of first place in the AFC West after allowing the Broncos to score 15 unanswered fourth-quarter points. That said, the Jets shouldn't present the same level of resistance. Kansas City is 2-1 ATS at Arrowhead, while the Jets are 2-1-1 ATS on the road. The total for this game opened at 43.5 but has since moved up to 45.5. The Under is 2-1 in Chiefs home games this season. The Giants were on the bye in Week 8, so they'll be well rested for this NFC East road matchup in Philly. They'll enter Lincoln Financial Field as a 2.5-point favorite, which is up from the 1.5 points they were laying at the open. New York is 5-2 ATS entering Week 9, which includes a 2-1 ATS record on the road. Philadelphia is 0-3 ATS as a home underdog in 2026. Houston picked up a point and a half and are laying 4.5 points on the road to the Chargers after initially opening as a field goal favorite. LA remains winless on the season after falling to the Rams on Sunday. It is 0-1 ATS as a home underdog this season and 0-3 ATS at home overall. The Texans are 1-1 ATS on the road. The total sits at 42.5, and the Under could be a popular play, with it owning a 6-1 record in Chargers games this season. New England is a 2.5-point favorite at home over the Packers, who'll have a rest advantage after playing last Thursday. New England is 3-4-1 ATS this season, which includes a 2-1 ATS record at home. As for the Packers, they're 2-2 ATS on the road this season (5-3 ATS overall). The Under is 3-1 in Packers road games entering Week 9. Seattle is an 11.5-point favorite despite squaring off against Arizona after playing on a short week. Given that the Seahawks still have their Week 8 matchup with the Bears to play on Monday night, this line could see movement once that game goes final. Arizona is coming off an upset win on the road against Dallas, improving to 4-1 ATS on the road this season. One thing worth monitoring with the Cardinals is their situation at quarterback. Jacoby Brissett was benched for Gardner Minshew on Sunday, so it'll be interesting to see how Mike LaFleur approaches the position going forward. San Francisco emerges from the bye week as a 9.5-point favorite over the Raiders. The Niners are 2-2 ATS at home this season with an average margin of victory of 11 points. Meanwhile, the Raiders are 3-1 ATS on the road this season, and that 75% cover rate is tied for the third-highest in the NFL. The total, which sits at 51.5 for this game, is 6-2 in Raiders games this season and 3-4 in Niners games. picks.blurb: Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Jaguars vs. Ravens bold predictions for Week 9 Thursday Night Football Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 10:16 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's a strange injury-marred matchup between the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens . It's especially tough as the Ravens got hit at the QB position . But these teams meet in Week 9 on Thursday Night Football, and here are bold predictions. Life is better for the Jaguars. They're in the weaker AFC South division. They have a record of 5-2 and a three-game lead over the second-place Texans. Meanwhile, the Ravens are 4-4. That's worth last place in the tougher AFC North. It's a desperation game for the Ravens. Can they come up with a plan to move the football? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten will rush for 100-plus yards The Ravens have a fairly solid run defense. But there's a caveat to this prediction. The Jaguars won't need a lot of points to win this game. The Ravens will struggle to put points on the board as the Jaguars stack the box against Derrick Henry. That means the Jaguars will be content to pound the ground game once they get a double-digit lead. And that means more carries for Tuten. He's coming off a 104-yard rushing performance against the Colts. And he should hit the mark again. Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said he liked what he saw from Tuten, according to jacksonville.com. "I thought Tuten played really well (against the Colts)," Coen said. "He was seeing it. I thought he was a little more patient in this game. He was running through contact. He was explosive in the passing game. Tuten had a great week of practice, and it really carried over." Tuten said things fell into place , according to ESPN. "We knew it was going to rain," Tuten said. "We knew we were going to run the ball, and we just went out and imposed our will." Things are set up nicely for Tuten to have another big game. Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence will throw three TD passes Even if Tuten runs up and down the field, the Ravens will commit to stopping him inside the 10-yard line. That will open up opportunities for Lawrence to complete drives with TD passes. This season, Lawrence has 17 touchdown passes with four interceptions. And Lawrence is trying to keep the Jaguars in all-business mode , according to news4jax.com. "Winning your division is really important, but I think for us, it's really just going week by week," Lawrence said. "It's not something we think, 'Oh, we're a few games up. We're in a good spot. We can relax.' That's not really at all how we think. We got a lot of football left." The Ravens have two choices on defense. They can take chances and try to create splash plays. Or they can sit back and try to keep the game close, where they could steal one in the fourth quarter. If they take chances against Lawrence, he will simply hit them with longer strikes. It seems like a no-win situation for the Ravens. And a big day for Lawrence and the Jaguars. Ravens RB Derrick Henry will set season high in carries Make no doubt about it. The Ravens are going to put a saddle on Henry and try to ride him to a victory. Henry has 24 carries twice this year. But his season high of 26 came against the Cowboys in overtime. Look for him to eclipse that number. That is, if the Ravens can keep the ball long enough for him to rack up carries while the game is still within reach. But it's possible the Ravens will feed Henry even if they fall behind by two scores. That's all because the only real path to a win is through Henry. Henry has been the recent subject of trade rumors because of the injury to Jackson. The Giants have been in that conversation, but head coach John Harbaugh said it's hard to make big trades , according to Giants.com. "We're going to do the most we can possibly do to try to get some things done," Harbaugh said. "It's hard to get deals done. It's hard. You can see how hard it is, but we're going to do our best and what's for our team. And the best thing we can do, the main thing we're going to do is focus on our guys and get ready to play the game. But all that other stuff is definitely going on behind the scenes at all times." For now, Henry remains with the Ravens. And he has to be their leader on Thursday night. away.blurb: The Jaguars officially ruled defensive back Antonio Johnson out for Sunday's game vs. the Colts , with the fourth-year safety set to miss the AFC South battle due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 6 in London against the Houston Texans. Johnson has not practiced for the Jaguars this week, being listed as a non-particpant in all three practices. With Johnson officially out on Sunday, the Jaguars will more than likely turn to safety Kaevon Merriweather to start against the Colts, but who exactly is the veteran safety and what does he bring to the table? The Jaguars have seen their safety group get hit with injuries at different points this season, and Merriweather has been one veteran who has helped steady the waters. The fourth-year safety signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2023 and appeared in 42 games with the Buccaneers in three seasons. This included 14 games with the Buccaneers in 2024 when Jaguars head coach Liam Coen was the team's offensive coordinator. “Need Kaevon to continue to step up and evolve. But being with him in Tampa, he was a guy that really helped on teams and played his tail off there but was also able to step in and he started, I think, like eight games for us that year in ‘24 at safety. The game wasn't too big for him," Coen said on Friday. Merriweather also spent time with the Houston Texans and Detroit Lions during parts of his career, and he signed to the Jaguars practice squad early in September. He was eventually moved up to the active roster, and he now looks like he will have to play a significant role in some facet against the Colts at home on Sunday. "And then when you went and watched him transition to Houston and then watched him throughout the preseason and the regular season on special teams, you could tell he took on some of the identity and ways in which Houston plays," Coen said. "That physicality, running to the football, burning it down and going and playing your ass off. That was something that was intriguing for us as well. away.blurb: Jaguars-Colts Thursday Injury Report: What Does Montaric Brown's Return Mean? - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL But what could the potential return of Brown really mean for the Jaguars in an important Week 8 AFC South battle? "Certainly, we'd have a guy who's got a lot of experience who knows our system. It'd be good to have him back out there healthy," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Thursday. "I know in the Philly game, tough situation where he got hurt there in the game, but he looks good and we gain a veteran presence, and we gain a level of physicality anytime Buster's out there," Campanile said. "I think he's done a great job for us that way on the line of scrimmage, tackling, being physical, even in the coverage element of everything. So yeah, that's what we gain with him in there." Getting Brown back at cornerback could allow the Jaguars to do a number of things differently, including getting Hunter more snaps on offense after his dominant game against the Houston Texans. Not having Brown available was the primary reason Hunter didn't play an offensive snap in Week 4 against the Bengals, which to date is the only game in Hunter's career in which he did not take a snap on both sides of the ball. Getting Brown back also happens at a good time for the secondary since safety Antonio Johnson did not practice for the second day in a row with an ankle injury. Johnson looks unlikely to play against the Colts, which means the Jaguars will need backups like Kaevon Merriweather and reinforcements like Brown to step up in the secondary. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Wednesday Injury Report: It Is Time to Unleash Jalen Huskey
away.blurb: Johnson was the only Jaguar who did not practice Wednesday, which is not a great sign coming off a bye week. Johnson injured his ankle in the Week 6 loss to the Houston Texans in London, and the Jaguars very well may be without their best safety once they kick off against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. Limited in practice for the Jaguars were four players: linebacker Jalani Tavai (hamstring), wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring), long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder), and defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro. Jaguars-Colts Wednesday Injury Report: It Is Time to Unleash Jalen Huskey Skip to main content SI.COM JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- There should be one clear reaction to the Jacksonville Jaguars' first injury report of Week 8: it is time for Jalen Huskey. Huskey, the No. 100 pick in April's NFL Draft, has yet to log a snap on defense and has only been active for one game. But the Jaguars should use this week to push Huskey toward some real playing time considering starting safety Antonio Johnson missed Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury. With second-year safety Caleb Ransaw on injured reserve and not looking close to returning anytime soon, the Jaguars' options at safety while Johnson recovers are starting safety Eric Murray, backup safety Kaevon Merriweather, second-year special teamer Rayuan Lane, or Huskey. The Jaguars leaned toward Merriweather getting playing time over Huskey at previous points, but it is time for the Jaguars to unleash their rookie. Merriweather has played 45 NFL games and has been in the NFL since 2023, so naturally he has more experience than Huskey does just a few months into his NFL career. But the Jaguars need to see what they have in their young safety, especially as injuries continue to hit the safety room. Even if the Jaguars start Merriweather over Huskey, they should deploy their third-round defensive back as their No. 3 safety. Simply put, Jacksonville has a young, athletic and talented safety who has been waiting in the wings, and it is time to see what he has. That is not to say Huskey would be the solution to the Jaguars' issues with explosive passes allowed, but he would give the Jaguars a dynamic at the safety position that Lane and Merriweather likely would not. Johnson not playing on Sunday would be a significant blow for the Jaguars' defense considering the impact he has made this season, both in coverage and as a blitzer against the run and rushing the passer. Cincinnati arrives at 5-2 after a wild overtime win over the Titans, while Atlanta is 3-5 and coming off a rain-soaked shutout loss in Tampa Bay. The Bengals are 3-point favorites, with the total at 52.5. The Bengals didn’t score in the first quarter and trailed 13-0, before Joe Burrow took over. He went 38 of 48 for 462 yards and five touchdowns, although he also threw three interceptions and lost a fumble, so it wasn’t a clean day. Tee Higgins was the standout, with 10 catches for 155 yards and two touchdowns. That followed a 35-13 win over the Ravens in Week 7, and at 5-2, the Bengals’ offense is as dangerous as any in the league when Burrow gets going. The concern is on the other side of the ball. Cincinnati gave up 36 points to a 1-7 Titans team, with Cameron Ward throwing for 304 yards and Tony Pollard running for 117 yards and two scores. Atlanta’s 16-0 loss in Tampa Bay is a hard game to read too much into. The rain was so heavy that the Buccaneers didn’t complete a single pass, with Baker Mayfield going 0 for 3, and Tampa Bay simply handed the ball to Bucky Irving, who ran for 170 yards and a touchdown. Michael Penix Jr. struggled badly in the conditions, going 8 of 24 for 125 yards with four interceptions, and Bijan Robinson was held to 76 yards on 19 carries. At 3-5, the Falcons need a performance. Sunday’s forecast in Madrid is for some light rain, nothing like last week’s downpour, so Penix should get a fairer chance to throw the ball. Still, this is an offense that has to prove it can score consistently, and Atlanta’s run defense will have questions to answer after the way Irving ran through it. Bengals vs Falcons Predictions There’s no real home-field edge at a neutral site, so the Bengals are favored on talent alone, and I think that’s the right side. Cincinnati’s offense put up 43 points last week even with four turnovers, and with Burrow throwing to Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase, the Bengals have far more ways to score than an Atlanta offense still looking for answers. I took the Bengals at -3.5, where they needed to win by four. The move to -3 is good news if you’re betting it now, because three is the most common winning margin in the NFL, and at -3 a three-point Bengals win is a push rather than a loss. At 52.5, the market is expecting points, and that makes sense given the Bengals have been involved in some high-scoring games. But international games have had a small lean towards the under, which is 30-26 across the last 56, and the only previous game at the Bernabéu also stayed under. A 9:30 AM ET kickoff plays its part, with both teams adjusting to a body clock that feels like mid-afternoon in Europe and early morning back home. We saw last week how slowly the Bengals can start, with no points in the first quarter, and even light rain can take a little off both passing games. I took the under at 51.5, and the move to 52.5 only gives anyone betting it now an extra point to work with. You can’t keep asking the offense to win every game by putting up 35 or 40 points. Eventually, that’s going to catch up with you. What I do like is that Cincinnati has already shown it can respond when things get uncomfortable. That Tennessee game wasn’t pretty, but the Bengals found a way to win. away.blurb: Kyle Dugger (quad) continues to not practice as he heads toward another missed game this week. Fellow safety Jordan Battle was also limited again with a shoulder injury, but he's been playing through that issue in outings over the last few weeks. On the Titans' side of things, starting defensive tackle John Franklin-Meyers (groin) upgraded to limited and starting receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) did not practice for a second-straight day. Bengals Injury Report: Ja'Marr Chase's Status Upgraded on Thursday as Bengals Continue Titans Preparation Skip to main content SI.COM The Bengals dropped their Thursday injury report ahead of the Titans game, and Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) got upgraded to full status on the report after not practicing due to that small issue and rest in general on Wednesday. He told the media on Thursday his ankle feels fine. Cincinnati is pretty clean besides those names. Cincinnati head coach Zac Taylor has had to shuffle around his tight end room due to all of the injuries in recent weeks. Erick All just went on season-ending injured reserve with a torn ACL, and fellow tight end Tanner Hudson tore a pec this season as well. "Attention to detail has been really important to him," Taylor said about rookie tight end Jack Endries as he gets primed for more snaps. "Waiting for his moment, you can tell he never knew when his number was going to be called. He's really got to know three different positions and so I've got trust, just watching him operate in practice and in meetings and in training camp, that if needed, he was going to be ready to go, and there was a time where he wasn't needed because we had everybody healthy, and now's that time. So I'm not nervous at all about using him. I think he's earning the opportunity. I'm excited to watch him play." Taylor also echoed confidence in backup safety PJ Jules, who is filling in for Dugger's reserve role. "PJ brings a lot of energy. It's really important to him," Taylor noted. "He's done a great job on special teams in his roles. He stepped into safety. So when we need to continue to rely on depth at the safety position, I feel very confident in PJ and Russ (Yeast)." away.headline: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans
away.blurb: Bengals officially declare one player out, another questionable for Week 8 matchup against Titans Skip to content The Cincinnati Bengals released their third and final injury report ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Tennessee Titans. Cincinnati has officially declared one player out, and another questionable for Sunday's game against Tennessee. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) is officially out, and linebacker Joe Giles-Harris (calf) is officially questionable against the Titans. Coach Zac Taylor said at the beginning of the week Dugger would not play and is “week-to-week” after aggravating his calf injury last week against the Baltimore Ravens. Giles-Harris figures to be a game-time decision, and his status may be foreshadowed depending on whether or not the club elevates LB Emany Johnson off the practice squad Saturday. As expected, Ja'Marr Chase (ankle) is good to play despite missing Wednesday. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen, B.J. Hill, and Dexter Lawrence II all had standard rest days. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee), wide receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), and punter Tommy Townsend (left knee) have all been declared out. None of them practiced at all this week, including Tate, the former Ohio State Buckeye and No. 4 overall pick from the 2026 NFL Draft. WR Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable. Assuming he plays, it'll be him, Elic Ayomanor, and Wan'Dale Robinson leading quarterback Cam Ward's passing attack with Tate sidelined. Starting tight end Gunnar Helm may also see a rise in involvement. He caught four passes for 24 yards last week against the Cleveland Browns. DT John Franklin-Myers (groin) is also questionable, along with cornerback Jaylon Jones (knee), and LB Dorian Mausi (foot). Mausi is still on the Reserve/Injured list and is ineligible to play unless Tennessee activates him to its 53-man roster. The Cincinnati Bengals are riding high after their second consecutive victory. They'll look to make it three in a row as they return home to face the Tennessee Titans. away.headline: Ja’Marr Chase injury update is concerning start to week for Bengals WR
away.blurb: Meyers has been the most productive of that group, with the rookie posting 141 yards. He would serve as Cincinnati's No. 2 in the receivers room if Chase is ruled out. Ja’Marr Chase injury update is concerning start to week for Bengals WR - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Ja’Marr Chase injury update is concerning start to week for Bengals WR Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads It appears Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase is on injury watch at the outset of Week 8. According to Bengals reporter Mike Petraglia , Chase was not spotted at practice during the portion open to the media on Wednesday. "Bengals stretch on a perfect Wednesday outside Paycor. No Ja'Marr Chase spotted at stretch," Petraglia wrote. This means that Chase is on track to be a non-participant in practice to begin the week, which puts his status in question. MORE: NFL MVP odds entering Week 8 As of this writing, it isn't clear what Chase is dealing with that has him sidelined. The superstar wide receiver was not listed on Cincinnati's injury report last week. We'll have our answer later in the day, when the Bengals release their first injury report. The good news is, Chase will have two more days to get back on the practice field and avoid a designation before the Bengals host the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Bengals' shaky wide receiver depth Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (5). Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect. If Chase keeps trending in the wrong direction, it's going to take a village to replace one of the league's best wideouts. The problem, however, is that the Bengals don't have many reliable villagers. Tee Higgins is rock-solid and would step into the role as the Bengals' No. 1 wide receiver if Chase is forced to sit. Higgins is having a phenomenal season with 571 receiving yards and two scores in six games. He has been especially hot of late after tallying 11 catches for 157 yards in Week 4 and six catches for 148 yards and a touchdown in Week 7 MORE: NFL could learn something from MLB's success with ABS Higgins ranks eighth in the NFL in receiving yards and has more than Chase, who has 351 in six contests. The problem is: who steps up behind him? Andrei Iosivas is on injured reserve , and the Bengals have a slew of wild cards in their receivers room with guys like Dohnte Meyers, Colbie Young and Mitch Tinsley. Along with Higgins and Meyers, the Bengals will also need more from tight end Mike Gesicki, who ranks third on the team in receiving yards with 165. The Bengals and Titans meet at 1 p.m. ET Sunday on CBS and Paramount+.

home.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
home.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). home.headline: Falcons-Bucs Inactives | Antoine Winfield Jr. Makes His Return
home.blurb: Tampa Bay Buccaneers safety Antoine Winfield Jr. has missed three games thanks to a rib injury suffered against Green Bay in Week Four, but he is cleared to play on Sunday against the Atlanta Falcons and expected to start. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, however, was ruled out on Friday and will be sidelined for the second game in a row by a foot injury. He had previously been listed with a concussion as well but was able to clear the league's concussion protocol late in the week. Tackle Luke Goedeke will also return to action after missing one game with a calf injury. Goedeke did not practice on Wednesday and Thursday but returned during Friday's session in a limited capacity. The Buccaneers and Falcons submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Eight meeting at Raymond James Stadium. The Buccaneers did not make any practice squad elevations this week and thus have 53 available players on Sunday, meaning they had to name five inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Falcons elevated linebacker Brian Asamoah and running back Khalil Herbert from their practice squad and therefore had to name seven players inactive for the game. Atlanta's offense will be without it's complementary backfield weapon for Bijan Robinson, as Brian Robinson is out due toa hamstring injury. Starting linebacker Divine Deablo will also miss the game due to a forearm injury, though fellow starter Kendal Daniels was cleared after missing some practice time due to an Achilles tendon ailment. Cornerback Billy Bowman will join Deablo on the sideline thanks to a hamstring strain, but cornerback Avieon Terrell, who was considered questionable for the game due to illness is good to go. home.headline: Falcons Have Another Lengthy Injury Report vs. Buccaneers, 1 Player Out Already
home.blurb: Falcons Have Another Lengthy Injury Report vs. Buccaneers, 1 Player Out Already Skip to main content SI.COM The Falcons officially ruled out running back Brian Robinson Jr. on Friday due to a hamstring injury, marking his second consecutive absence. Khalil Herbert will be his likely replacement after a good showing last week in a win over the 49ers. Robinson has not been able to return to the field since suffering the injury, leaving Atlanta without one of its primary options behind Bijan Robinson. While Robinson is the only player officially ruled out, the Falcons have several other injury concerns heading into Sunday’s divisional matchup. Eight players are listed as questionable, including three defensive players who could have significant roles against Tampa Bay. Defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and Avieon Terrell are both questionable. Bowman is dealing with a hamstring injury, while Terrell has been working through an illness. Both players missed Atlanta’s victory over San Francisco last week. Linebacker Divine Deablo is also questionable with a forearm injury. His potential absence would be notable for Atlanta’s defense, as Deablo has served as one of the unit’s primary communicators this season. The remaining questionable players include wide receivers Beaux Collins (hip) and Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), defensive ends Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and Charles Snowden (back), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle). There is some encouraging news for Atlanta heading into the weekend. Collins and Williams both participated fully in Friday’s practice, while the other questionable players were limited participants. The Falcons have no players listed as doubtful. Falcons Rule Out Two Key Defensive Starters Ahead of Buccaneers Showdown The Atlanta Falcons will be without another key offensive player when they travel to Tampa to face the Buccaneers in Week 8. Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading the rushing attack, but losing another running back limits Atlanta’s depth at the position. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels stepped into a larger role against the 49ers and delivered one of the biggest performances of his young career. Daniels helped seal the victory with a late interception of Brock Purdy. Atlanta will need as many healthy players as possible against a Tampa Bay team coming off a convincing 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers. The Buccaneers enter Sunday’s matchup looking to build on that performance, while the Falcons are coming off a 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated 49ers. Atlanta and Tampa Bay will meet Sunday, Nov. 1, at Raymond James Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jon Spradley · SB Nation Mon, November 2, 2026 at 12:24 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts return home after a brutal two-game road trip. The Colts just completed their annual beatdown at the hands of the Jaguars and are hoping home has some better results. The Cowboys are licking their own wounds and will be in fight mode to save their season. FanDuel Sportsbook is giving the Cowboys all the love as the Colts are 5.5-point underdogs. The money line is +220 and the over/under is 52.5. What is there to say? Going on the road against the Jaguars has been the Colts' kryptonite. Before things kicked off, it didn't seem like this was the year the losing streak was going to end. All that game ended was a few more players' careers as Colts. Turnovers, missed tackles, and a team that looks like it has thrown in the towel was on the field this week. It was 35-0 before the Colts decided to score. That's all you really need to know about this one. Dallas seemed to have their high-scoring affair under wraps with less than four minutes left in the fourth. Up ten wasn't enough, however, as the Cardinals scored a game-tying touchdown with ten seconds left. They gave the Cowboys a gift by missing the extra point and sending this one into overtime. Both teams got a possession in overtime, but the Cardinals got the last laugh with a game-winning field goal. Neither team is feeling good about their season. Dallas still has hope though. Expect Lucas Oil to be full of Cowboys fans as they travel well, and the Colts fans might have already thrown in the towel. If the Colts are going to get things right, it has to be this one. If not here, it might not happen this year at all.

(2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The bigger issues for Indianapolis are on the offensive side of the ball where the Colts average just 20.1 points per game. Yes, it seemed obvious the Colts were waving the white flag following midweek trades of DeForest Buckner and Quentin Nelson but to make sure there was no doubt of their intentions, they endured a smack from Jacksonville on Sunday, 42-7. The Jaguars led 28-0 at halftime and finished with 366 total yards, while the Colts’ offensive woes were on full display turning the ball over three times and amassing a mere 243 yards. Daniel Jones endured a particularly rough afternoon, finishing 19-of-28 for 144 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, including a 92-yard pick-six, before Anthony Richardson replaced him late. Reports Monday indicated that Jones is expected to remain the starter against Dallas, with Richardson staying in the backup role. Sunday’s game is beyond a must-win for Dallas if they are to continue to entertain any hopes of even competing for a playoff spot. The Colts’ offense has been pedestrian on its better days, but the Cowboys have made even bad offenses look elite. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. FOX has the broadcast, and the Cowboys are favored by 5.5 points, with the total at 51.5. That’s a pretty high total for a matchup involving a Colts team that just scored seven points. Then again, Dallas just gave up 33 to Arizona, so maybe the sportsbooks know something about these defenses. Both teams are coming off losses, and somebody needs to figure out how to stop the other team from moving the football. Check out our free NFL picks for more predictions. Dallas Cowboys Have Been Scoring but Giving Up Too Much Dallas is 3-5 after losing 33-30 to Arizona in overtime on Sunday. That’s a frustrating way to lose, especially when you’ve scored 30 points at home. The Cowboys had beaten Philadelphia 38-21 the previous week, so the offense has been doing its job lately. Sixty-eight points in two games should be enough to win both. Instead, Dallas split them. The problem is the defense. You can’t keep giving up big plays and expecting the offense to bail you out. Arizona moved the ball well enough to score 33, and now Dallas is heading into another road game. Indianapolis hasn’t been particularly dangerous offensively, but the Cowboys have made life easier for opponents who probably shouldn’t be scoring as much as they are. Still, I like Dallas’ chances of moving the football Sunday. The Cowboys have scored at least 30 points in consecutive games, and Indianapolis just got embarrassed by Jacksonville. If Dallas gets into a rhythm early, the Colts could have a difficult time keeping up. That’s especially true if Indianapolis has to abandon its running game and start chasing points. Indianapolis Colts Need to Forget About Jacksonville Indianapolis is 2-6 after losing 42-7 to Jacksonville last Sunday. That’s the kind of game where you probably don’t want to watch the film more than once. The Colts also lost 16-10 to Minnesota the previous week, so they’ve scored just 17 points over their last two games. That’s not going to get it done against many NFL teams. The defense has been a major concern, too. Giving up 42 points to Jacksonville is bad enough, but now Indianapolis has to face a Dallas offense that’s been putting up some pretty good numbers. The Colts need to make the Cowboys work for their points instead of giving away easy scoring opportunities. If Dallas starts hitting big plays, this could get ugly. Here’s the one thing that gives Indianapolis a chance. Dallas has been allowing plenty of points itself. The Colts don’t need to be perfect to find some success against that defense. If Indianapolis can run the football, keep the game close, and avoid turnovers, it might be able to hang around. But after scoring seven against Jacksonville, I’m not ready to trust the Colts to do enough offensively. Dallas Cowboys vs Indianapolis Colts Picks and Prediction Spread Pick: Dallas Cowboys -5.5 I’m laying the 5.5 with Dallas. I don’t love backing a 3-5 team on the road, but Indianapolis has been even worse. The Colts just lost by 35 points and have scored only 17 over their last two games. Dallas, meanwhile, has scored 68 in its last two. That’s a pretty significant difference. The Cowboys’ defense worries me, and I wouldn’t be surprised if Indianapolis finds some success against it. But I think Dallas has enough offense to pull away. Give me the Cowboys by a touchdown or more. Total Pick: Over 51.5 I’ll take the over 51.5, but this one comes with some risk. Dallas has been involved in some high-scoring games lately, and its defense just gave up 33 to Arizona. The Cowboys can probably get into the 30s against Indianapolis, which gives us a good start. The question is whether the Colts can contribute enough. Scoring seven against Jacksonville doesn’t inspire confidence, but Dallas has been allowing opponents to move the football. If Indianapolis gets into the low 20s, I think we have a good chance. Something like 34-21 would get us there. away.headline: Cowboys Injury Report: Luke Schoonmaker Added Thursday
away.blurb: FRISCO, Texas — Luke Schoonmaker did not practice Thursday for the Dallas Cowboys , who added the tight end to their injury report with a groin injury three days before the Arizona Cardinals visit AT&T Stadium. Four players were limited on both days. Rookie safety Caleb Downs (ankle) and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams (hamstring) were new to the report this week. Wide receiver George Pickens is listed with shoulder and hamstring injuries, and rookie tackle Drew Shelton is still working back from a hamstring injury that kept him out of the last two games. Turpin, Winters, and Shelton were all inactive Monday when the Cowboys ran for 204 yards in a 38-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles . Tyler Goodson took the kickoffs in Turpin’s place. His 99-yard return for a touchdown came back on a holding penalty. “It was great playing, number-one. A lot like Dee Winters last week. The catch was awesome. Put us into a four-minute situation, and it was awesome to see him back out there along with Cobie Durant,” Schottenheimer said after the game. Thumb surgery before the opener cost Smith the first four games. Dallas opened the All-Pro left guard’s return window Oct. 5, three days before a Thursday night home game. Downs went No. 11 overall in April after Dallas traded up one spot to take him out of Ohio State. Williams came over from the New York Jets at last season’s trade deadline. Pickens had 4 catches for 57 yards and a touchdown on 6 targets Monday, scoring from 21 yards out before halftime. home.blurb: Sunday’s matchup at Lucas Oil Stadium brings together two teams badly in need of a reset, as the Dallas Cowboys (3-5) visit the Indianapolis Colts (2-6) at 1 p.m. ET. Dallas is coming off a crushing 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona in which it led 24-10 early in the fourth quarter and 30-24 in the final minute, only for Gardner Minshew to lead an 80-yard game-tying touchdown drive before Chad Ryland won it with a 42-yard field goal in overtime. Dak Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown and added a five-yard rushing score, but Dallas managed only 261 total yards and went three-and-out on its lone overtime possession. The loss dropped the Cowboys to 3-5 and magnified a season-long problem: the defense. Dallas is allowing 26.6 points and 385.4 yards per game. The most recent meeting between these teams produced one of the wildest quarters in Cowboys’ history. On December 4, 2022, Indianapolis trailed 21-19 entering the fourth quarter in Arlington before Dallas erupted for 33 unanswered points to win 54-19. Prescott threw three touchdown passes, Tony Pollard ran for 91 yards and two scores, and the Cowboys forced five turnovers, including Malik Hooker’s 38-yard fumble-return touchdown against his former team. The recent series has otherwise gone back and forth: Indianapolis shut out Dallas 23-0 in 2018, Dallas won 42-7 in 2014, the Cowboys earned a 38-35 overtime victory in 2010, and Dallas won 21-14 in 2006. Erickson Indianapolis Star Oct. 29, 2026, 5:23 p.m. ET The Indianapolis Colts have made several roster changes due to injuries, particularly at cornerback and linebacker. Rookie linebacker CJ Allen is expected to start after recovering from an ankle injury, leading to the release of veteran Germaine Pratt. Cornerback Sauce Gardner returned to full practice, offering a potential solution to injuries in the secondary. INDIANAPOLIS — The Colts have made a flurry of roster moves this week, trying to cover a rash of injuries at the cornerback position while shoring up depth at linebacker. Rookie middle linebacker CJ Allen was a full participant in practice for the second consecutive day after missing last week’s game due to an ankle injury, although his fellow rookie, Bryce Boettcher, missed his second consecutive day with a groin injury. Indianapolis feels confident enough in its linebacker group to release veteran Germaine Pratt, who was signed to the practice squad two weeks ago but no longer has a path to playing time. Pratt played 20 snaps against Minnesota this week due to injuries, but the Colts plan to move Allen into the starting lineup now that he’s healthy. Pratt was a starter for 12 games in Indianapolis in 2025; the Colts are trying to get younger and faster at the position. “C.J. was going to start this week before he had that injury,” defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said. “I think they’re all putting their time in, and the more at bats they get, the better they’re going to be.” The Colts have larger issues at cornerback. Sauce Gardner practiced in full for the first time since suffering a calf injury against Tennessee, offering a potential starting option. Indianapolis placed Cam Taylor-Britt on injured reserve earlier this week, and Justin Walley missed the second consecutive day with a knee injury. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 9 Survivor Pool Picks Kansas City Chiefs The Kansas City Chiefs have some issues finishing drives when they take on the elite teams in the NFL, but based on their running game and defense alone, they're well-suited to crush inferior teams. They'll host the New York Jets in Week 9, who can't beat the likes of the Miami Dolphins or Las Vegas Raiders. The Jets' defense has been especially bad this season, ranking 24th in opponent success rate. It's also worth noting that Kansas City doesn't have many more games this season that will make sense for Survivor. A home game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 11 is the other option, but at this point, I believe in the Jets a lot less than Arizona. Indy was blown out by the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8 – 42-7 – and it’s a candidate to move on from more pieces ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts haven’t been a competitive team for most of this season, starting with a 2-6 record while ranking 29th in EPA/Play on offense and 23rd in EPA/Play on defense. The Dallas defense can’t stop anyone, ranking 32nd in EPA/Play and 30th in yards per play allowed, but this offense is still elite. The Cowboys put up 30 points once again in Week 8 against Arizona, and they’re a top-10 team in EPA/Play and success rate on that side of the ball. Dak Prescott should be able to move the ball pretty easily against a Colts defense that couldn’t slow down Trevor Lawrence (three passing scores) and the Jaguars in Week 8. Indy is an easy team to fade the rest of the season with Daniel Jones clearly in over his head at quarterback. Jones has five touchdown passes, nine picks and has only completed 60.4 percent of his passes. If Dallas can’t win this game, the NFC East crown may truly be out of reach. This week the Las Vegas Raiders broke their own four game losing streak by out-scoring the Jets in a wild 38 – 33 shootout in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The Jets took a nine point lead into the locker room at halftime, only to unravel in the second half. The Jets defense was helpless to stop the Raiders attack in the second half as the Jets were out-scored 24 – 10 to close the game. It was a humiliating performance by a putrid Jets defense. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The New York Jets head to Arrowhead Stadium on Sunday, November 8, trying to keep their season from slipping further away against a Kansas City Chiefs team that is looking to halt a skid of its own. The Jets have lost three straight. They are 2-6 overall (1-3 on the road) and in the cellar in the AFC East. The Chiefs are 3-0 at home and 5-2 overall but have lost two in a row and sit in second in the AFC West a ½ game behind the Broncos. The Jets are coming off a frustrating 38-33 home loss to the Raiders in which they produced plenty of offense but couldn’t stop Vegas late. New York scored on its first six possessions, led 23-14 at halftime and 30-21 during the third quarter, but Las Vegas rallied with back-to-back touchdown drives to take a lead late. Geno Smith threw for 290 yards, two touchdowns and an interception, while Braelon Allen rushed for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown and Adonai Mitchell produced a career-best 142 receiving yards with a score. A big red flag for the Jets continues to be their inefficiency in the red zone on offense and defense: New York went just 2-for-6 in the red zone while Las Vegas finished 4-for-4. Kansas City also melted late in their game last Sunday against the Broncos, blowing a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss at Denver. Patrick Mahomes played much better than he had in the Chiefs’ previous defeat at Seattle, completing 30 of 41 passes for 321 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, including a 73-yard touchdown to Emmett Johnson . Denver, however, scored 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter, Harrison Butker missed a 54-yard field goal, and after Mahomes drove the Chiefs inside the Broncos’ 5 in the final minute, Denver made a goal-line stand capped by Malcolm Roach’s sack on fourth down. Historically, the matchup has produced some memorable games. The most recent meeting was a few years ago on October 1, 2023, when Kansas City escaped MetLife Stadium with a 23-20 win. The Chiefs raced ahead 17-0 in the first quarter before the Jets rallied to tie the game at 20 behind Zach Wilson , who completed 28 of 39 passes for 245 yards and two touchdowns. Mahomes had an unusually uneven passing night, finishing 18 of 30 for 203 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions, but Kansas City retook the lead on Butker’s 26-yard field goal and Mahomes used his legs to help drain the clock late. That game offers a useful blueprint for Sunday’s upset-minded Jets: withstand Kansas City’s early punch, keep Mahomes from creating explosives and turn offensive production into touchdowns rather than field goals. For the Chiefs, the larger storyline is whether they can rediscover their finishing touch after consecutive losses on the road. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. away.blurb: Las Vegas appears to be getting healthier after several players participated in Wednesday's practice on a limited basis: Kwity Paye, DJ Glaze, Brock Bowers, Folorunso Fatukasi, Ian Thomas, and Quay Walker. Patrick Johnson did not participate in Wednesday's practice. On Friday, Jack Bech was added to the injury report, despite practicing every day this week. He is listed as questionable for Sunday's game. Johnson was ruled out for Sunday's game, as was Runyon. Veteran cornerback Eric Stokes was added to the report with an illness on Friday after not appearing on the injury report at all this week. Stokes participated on a limited basis in Friday's practice. Stokes is Las Vegas' best cornerback. Stokes' illness could negatively impact an already questionable group of defensive backs. Beyond Stokes' illness, Las Vegas also has unanswered questions elsewhere in its defensive backfield, as it tries to decide who the best option is to play alongside Stokes: Hezekiah Masses or Darien Porter. According to Kubiak, Powers-Johnson is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets. Las Vegas needs help at the guard position but also has to consider moves that could make them better moving forward as the trade deadline approaches. The Detroit Lions (5-2) will travel to Florida to take on the Miami Dolphins (1-6) in Week 9, in a battle between teams at two very different stages of their roster development. While the Lions are shaking off some early-season mistakes, they’ve strung together three wins, including back-to-back wins in their division, while the Dolphins are in the early stages of a rebuild under their latest regime. The folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions -7 points . The Dolphins made a general manager and head coaching change this offseason, firing GM Chris Grier and coach Mike McDaniel after four unsuccessful seasons and hiring Jon-Eric Sullivan as their new GM and former Green Bay Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley as their new coach. Like most new regimes, the new staff got to work early, cutting veteran contracts, including quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, wide receiver Tyreek Hill, and edge rusher Bradley Chubb. They also traded away former first-round pick Jaylen Waddle for a trio of picks to use in the 2026 NFL Draft to help them with the rebuild. Step one in establishing a new foundation was signing Malik Willis as their new signal caller—who most recently played in Green Bay with Hafley—and drafting six (!) rookie starters, including first-round picks guard Kadyn Proctor and corner Chris Johnson, as well as second-round pick linebacker Jacob Rodriguez, third-round receivers Chris Bell and Caleb Douglas, and fifth-round safety Michael Taaffe. They also have another eight rookies on their 53-man roster, meaning over 25% of the Dolphins roster (14 players) is made up of first-year players. As you would expect with a young roster at the beginning of a rebuild, the Dolphins have struggled out of the gate. In Week 1, the Raiders beat them by two touchdowns; the 49ers won by three touchdowns the week after; and the Chiefs beat them by two touchdowns in Week 3. In Week 4, they showed signs of improvement, losing to the Vikings by only five points; the Bengals won by just seven in Week 5, and in Week 6, they got their first win of the season, beating the Jets by three points. On Sunday, the Dolphins and Patriots squared off in an AFC East showdown, and while the Dolphins built a 13-3 lead at the half, the Patriots scored 21 unanswered points to go up 24-13 late in the fourth quarter. Willis connected on an explosive touchdown pass at the 2-minute warning to bring them close, but a failed 2-point conversion and a failed onside kick set the final score at 24-19. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. away.blurb: The team added that preliminary indications are positive, but no further information will be shared at this time out of respect for Campbell and his family. "Kevin O'Connell, man, he's a class act," Campbell said. "Looking out for him, checking in on Jack. I know those guys said a prayer for Jack. And that just says a lot about the humanity of it. A native of Cedar Falls, Iowa, Campbell broke out during his junior season with the Hawkeyes, totaling 143 tackles, two interceptions, two fumble recoveries and a sack in 2021. Returning for his senior season, Campbell was named an All-American in 2022 in addition to receiving the Butkus Award as the top linebacker in college football. Campbell slid right in as a key piece to the Lions defense following his arrival in the NFL. However, he didn't officially break out until his third season. Campbell recorded 176 total tackles, three forced fumbles and five sacks en route to being named a first-team All-Pro and earning his first Pro Bowl appearance last season. The quarterback pointed out that it isn't easy to get back into the game after a major injury like that. On Nov. 2, the team provided an update on Campbell . The Lions shared that Campbell is continuing to rest and recover, adding that preliminary tests are positive. Head coach Dan Campbell pointed to that update at his press conference , which began about 30 minutes after the team released the news. He also asked for continued prayers, saying that they are working and the news is positive. It was a press conference that came about 24 hours after Campbell, a linebacker and team captain, went down with the injury. Campbell laid motionless on the turf at Ford Field on Nov. 1 after making a tackle against a fellow former Iowa Hawkeye, T.J. Hockenson. Down for more than 10 minutes, the scene in Detroit served as a sobering reminder of just how violent and dangerous football can be. Campbell was immobilized, loaded onto a backboard and taken to the hospital, leading to an emotional on-field reaction from teammates . home.headline: Final Dolphins-Pats Injury Report: Proctor News Ends Remarkable Streak, Brown Remains a Mystery
home.blurb: Their season-opening streak of games with the same starting offensive line will end at six with the official Friday that rookie first-round pick Kadyn Proctor had been ruled out of the Week 8 game against the New England Patriots because of his concussion. This pretty much was a foregone conclusion once Proctor sat out practice Wednesday and Thursday, and it became official after he once again was a DNP on Friday. Proctor was the only member of the active roster who did not practice Friday and the only one who was so much as limited was long-snapper Tucker Addington, who continues to deal with a shoulder injury. Cornerback JuJu Brents was one of two players listed as questionable, but after being a full participant Friday, two days after missing practice with a concussion, it's a matter of getting final clearance over the weekend to play against New England and the outlook clearly is promising. Also listed as questionable was cornerback Reese Taylor, who has missed the past three games with a quad injury. Taylor had his first full practice in weeks Friday, though it should be pointed out that final practice of the week always is pretty light. New England didn't rule out anybody, which kind of comes as a bit of a surprise given the late-week developments involving wide receiver A.J. Brown. "Just like everything else, when you come out of the game or a long week or practice on Monday, you evaluate the player," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said. "He just wasn't able to practice or finish practice on Wednesday. So, we’ll continue to treat him, and then we'll see where he is (Saturday)." Running back TreVeyon Henderson missed practice for a second consecutive day because of illness and was listed as questionable, as were CB Carlton Davis III (neck) and LB Christian Elliss (chest). That season, the Dolphins opened with a starting five of (from left to right) Laremy Tunsil, Anthony Steen, Mike Pouncey, Jermon Bushrod and Ja'Wuan James until Steen was replaced by Jesse Davis in the seventh game. Since then, the Dolphins hadn't even gone five games at the start of a season with the same offensive line, reaching four games in 2020. And Dolphins fans surely remember last year when the Dolphins lost both James Daniels and Austin Jackson in the opener. So, yes, six games together for Patrick Paul, Proctor, Aaron Brewer, Jonah Savaiinaea and Jackson indeed was a big deal. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton Sunday’s Week 9 matchup at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. Plenty of positives happening with the Browns this season, but last week’s performance is not one of them. The Steelers thumped Cleveland, 27-6, in Pittsburgh. Cleveland was held without a touchdown for the first time this year, lost two fumbles, rushed for only 34 yards and surrendered eight sacks, while the Steelers piled up 200 yards and three touchdowns on the ground. Forced to throw for much of the afternoon, Deshaun Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards without an interception and Harold Fannin Jr. caught 10 passes for 154 yards. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. CBS has the broadcast, and the Saints are favored by 2.5 points despite having the worse record. The total is 43.5. That tells you something about how odd this matchup is. Cleveland has won five games, New Orleans has won two, and somehow the Browns are the underdogs. After watching Cleveland’s offense last weekend, I can understand why the sportsbooks aren’t particularly impressed. Check out our free NFL picks for more predictions. Cleveland Browns Need More From Their Offense Cleveland is 5-3 after getting beaten 27-6 by Pittsburgh on Sunday. Six points. That’s all the Browns could manage against a division rival, and there’s no way to make that sound encouraging. Cleveland had beaten Tennessee 27-24 the previous week, so the offense has shown it can produce. It just hasn’t been doing it consistently. The Browns are at their best when they can run the football, stay ahead of the chains, and let their defense put pressure on the opponent. That’s a pretty reasonable way to win games, especially against a New Orleans team that hasn’t been particularly convincing. But when Cleveland gets behind and has to throw on obvious passing downs, things become a lot more difficult. Here’s why I still like the Browns in this matchup. New Orleans isn’t Pittsburgh. The Saints have struggled to win games, and Cleveland has enough defensive ability to keep this close. The Browns don’t need to score 30 points to beat New Orleans. They just need to avoid another afternoon where the offense disappears completely. New Orleans Saints Have a Chance to Get Something Going New Orleans is 2-5 after having its bye last week. The Saints lost 16-10 to Pittsburgh in their most recent game, and before that they beat the Giants 34-27. That’s a pretty big difference in offensive production. One week they’re scoring 34, the next they’re struggling to reach double digits. The Saints have the advantage of playing at home, and they’ve had an extra week to prepare. That matters. New Orleans should have a chance to clean up some of the problems that showed up against Pittsburgh, particularly when it comes to sustaining drives. But an extra week doesn’t automatically fix an offense that’s been inconsistent. What concerns me about New Orleans is that Cleveland can make this a very uncomfortable game. The Browns have enough defensive talent to put pressure on the quarterback and force difficult throws. If the Saints can’t establish the run, they could end up in the same situation Cleveland found itself in last week. Lots of third-and-long situations and not enough points. Cleveland Browns vs New Orleans Saints Picks and Prediction Spread Pick: Cleveland Browns +2.5 I’m taking Cleveland and the points. I know the Browns looked terrible against Pittsburgh, but I’m not throwing away a 5-3 record because of one ugly afternoon. New Orleans is 2-5, and the Saints haven’t done enough to convince me they should be laying points against a team with Cleveland’s defensive ability. The extra preparation time helps New Orleans, but I think the Browns can keep this game close and possibly win outright. Give me Cleveland +2.5. Total Pick: Under 43.5 Give me the under 43.5. Cleveland just scored six points, and New Orleans managed only 10 in its last game. Both offenses have had better days, but neither has been consistent enough for me to expect a shootout. I think Cleveland tries to establish the run and keep the game manageable, while New Orleans looks to avoid mistakes against a capable Browns defense. The danger is a couple of short fields or defensive touchdowns pushing the score higher. Otherwise, this looks like the kind of game that could finish 20-17 or 21-20. away.blurb: Most notably, Browns defensive end Jared Verse (knee), who did not practice on Wednesday, was able to take part in a limited practice on Thursday. That's good news, as he absolutely has to be on the field for Sunday's game in Pittsburgh. After the Week 4 victory on a Thursday night, Verse endeared himself to Browns fans everywhere by trashing some of the Steelers players, calling them "dirty". He automatically gained likability among all Cleveland fans, as a result. Browns offensive tackle Tytus Howard (concussion) suffered a concussion in the Week 7 game against the Tennessee Titans, and he has not practiced this week in either session. That's the bad news. The good news is that he was the only 'DNP' for Thursday's practice. Rolling down the line, safety Grant Delpit (neck), defensive tackle Mason Graham (ankle), defensive tackle Mike Hall Jr. (ankle), cornerback Myles Harden (hamstring), center/offensive guard Elgton Jenkins (knee), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle), safety Daniel Thomas (ankle) and Verse were each limited participants on Thursday. After a limited practice on Thursday, running back Dylan Sampson (knee) was able to take part in a full practice session, and it appears he is trending toward another meaningful role in his second game back from the reserve/injured list. Gabriel was activated from the reserve/injured list, and he has been practicing in full for several weeks, as the Browns have figured out a way to keep all four quarterbacks without exposing any to the practice squad and/or having to lose them for the season on IR. home.blurb: Sunday’s Week 9 matchup at the Caesars Superdome brings together two teams in very different positions, as the Cleveland Browns (5-3) take the field against the New Orleans Saints (2-5). Cleveland is third in the AFC North but just one game behind the first place Steelers. New Orleans has lost four of their last five games and sit last in the NFC South but they are also only a game out of first as they return from their bye. The Superdome, however, has not been kind to the Saints who are winless in four home games (0-4). Cleveland, however, is a respectable 2-3 on the road this season. New Orleans has not played in a couple weeks, but their last game was also a loss to the Steelers, 16-10, in Paris on Oct. 25. The Saints managed only 18 rushing yards and were shut out in the second half, but quarterback Tyler Shough produced an encouraging performance through the air, completing 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards, one touchdown and one interception. It was symptomatic of the season to date: the offense has no balance. Historically, Cleveland leads the all-time series 13-7, but New Orleans has won each of the last three meetings, including the most recent matchup at this same venue on November 17, 2024. That game was tied 14-14 entering the fourth quarter before the Saints exploded for 21 unanswered points to win 35-14. Taysom Hill was the difference-maker, rushing seven times for 138 yards and three touchdowns, including fourth-quarter scoring runs of 33 and 75 yards, while Derek Carr threw for 248 yards and two touchdowns. Jameis Winston threw for 395 yards and two scores for Cleveland, but the Browns failed to turn their yardage into enough points. Two years later, the central question is similar for both clubs: which offense can translate production into touchdowns? Cleveland needs to protect Watson and rediscover a ground game that disappeared in Pittsburgh, while New Orleans needs Shough, Kamara and an offense coming out of the bye to take advantage of a Browns defense that just surrendered 200 rushing yards. Tyson's return could hurt Devaughn Vele the most. It looks like we could find out just how ready Tyson is for the NFL as soon as next week. The New Orleans Saints will be getting a reinforcement to their wide receivers room sooner rather than later, and that reinforcement is rookie Jordyn Tyson . According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Tyson, sidelined all season because of a hamstring injury, could play as soon as next week against the Cleveland Browns. Tyson was the Saints' No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. While there was never any doubt about his talent, there was uncertainty about his ability to stay healthy. The Arizona State product had injury issues in college, including with his hamstring, so he is obviously off to an ominous start in the NFL. Through the first seven games, Chris Olave has served as the Saints' No. 1, as expected, and he will continue to be quarterback Tyler Shough's top target. Olave leads the team with 49 catches and 636 receiving yards, and he has scored twice. The Eagles have a bye week following this NFC East clash, and I’m sure they feel it couldn’t come soon enough. Tanner McKee will make his fourth consecutive start after leading the Eagles to 14, 21, and 10 points. The offense has been injury-riddled. DeVonta Smith sat out and Saquon Barkley hobbled to 30 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. McCarthy . The New York offense has scored 27 points in each of the last two games and could’ve been 2-0. However, the Giants lost to the Saints 34-27 and beat the Texans 27-21 in OT before the bye week. New York has a rest advantage and likely a mental advantage over Philly. The Giants should be feeling good as they sit atop the NFC East, whereas the Eagles are at the bottom. Giants Add Familiar Face at Running Back as Skattebo’s Injury Status Raises Questions Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants were back to work on Monday after their Week 8 bye, but one key offensive player worked with trainers on the sideline during the media portion of practice. Running back Cam Skattebo, who said he felt something in his hamstring after his 42-yard run against the Houston Texans in overtime two weeks ago, was spotted working to the side with trainers. It’s unclear whether Skattebo is simply trying to buy a couple more days to let his hamstring fully heal before the team begins its prep for Sunday’s road game at Philadelphia, or whether the injury could limit him in practice and, potentially, the upcoming game. Head coach John Harbaugh characterized Skattebo's status as "day to day." Either way, the Giants, who last week placed running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with a hamstring injury, are not taking any chances of going into the critical division matchup with just Devin Singletary and newcomer Gregory Desrosiers, whom they signed last week off the Chargers’ practice squad. To that end, New York has signed running back Eric Gray, its fifth-round pick in the 2023 draft, to its practice squad. Gray, who was with the team this summer, appeared in 34 games over three seasons, including just four in 2025 after landing on PUP due to a knee injury. He has 31 career rushing attempts for 79 yards and caught 16 of 18 targets for 104 yards, with no rushing or receiving touchdowns. This past summer he led the team in receptions with eight catches for 54 yards. He also led the Giants in rushing with 90 yrds on 30 carries. Gray was with the Cleveland Browns practice squad in September but was released in early October. Despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart for the season in Week 2, the team is 4-2-1 and currently sits in first place in the NFC East. Gray is unlikely to step into a significant role, and Skattebo's status will likely become clearer as New York begins its official practice week and releases an injury report. In 2025, he missed training camp and the first 11 games of the regular season while on the Physically-Unable-to-Perform (PUP) list with a torn meniscus. He returned to play in four games, logging just three snaps on offense and 13 on special teams without recording a single offensive touch. The Giants had waived Gray in late August 2026. Ball security has remained a persistent issue for Gray, who has six career fumbles (two lost) on very limited touches. Gray possesses adequate short-area quickness and vision, but he lacks the top-end breakaway speed or physical strength needed to create yards after contact. home.headline: Saquon Barkley Injury Update: Eagles RB’s Week 8 Status Revealed
home.blurb: Saquon Barkley entered Week 7 with a hamstring injury that limited his workload against the Dallas Cowboys, and the running back suffered a back injury on Monday Night Football. Originally entering the league as the second-overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft , the Penn State product hit the ground running, recording 1,307 yards and 11 touchdowns as a rookie for the New York Giants. He remained an elite running back during his five years with the club before joining the Philadelphia Eagles in 2024, where he immediately led the league with 2,005 rushing yards while playing a key role in the team's championship run. After missing a few weeks of action, Saquon Barkley returned to the field in a limited role and finished Week 7's loss with seven carries for 62 yards and a touchdown to go along with two receptions for nine yards. While he only played nine snaps in the game thanks to the hamstring and back injuries, he will return to the field in Week 8. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Saquon Barkley is "good to go." Needless to say, this is great news for the Phialdelphia Eagles, as the entire offense is battling an absurd amount of injuries. Philadelphia's second- to fourth-string running backs are all injured, quarterback Jalen Hurts is out indefinitely, and wide receiver Devonta Smith will not play. Quite frankly, the Eagles have no choice but to run their offense through Barkley. Saquon Barkley is a great player, but he probably can't carry a team this banged-up to the postseason, especially with the starting quarterback sidelined for the rest of the season.
