home.headline: Cam Skattebo injury: Giants’ RB a question mark heading into game vs. Eagles
home.blurb: Even after the bye week, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo is still dealing with a hamstring injury he suffered during the team's Week 7 overtime win against the Houston Texans. Skattebo did not practice on Monday as the team returned to work. Skattebo broke off a 42-yard run in overtime that helped the Giants pull out a win, but it came at a price, as he picked up a hamstring injury. Giants head coach John Harbaugh spoke about Skattebo's injury in more detail. His struggles led to him being benched in the team's Week 6 loss against the New Orleans Saints, but he redeemed himself against the Texans when he had his best game of the season. He ran 17 times for 124 yards and a touchdown to help the Giants pull out a big win on the road. Should Skattebo have to sit out, it will mean an extended opportunity for Devin Singletary and newly-signed Gregory Desrosiers. Eric Gray, who was just signed to the practice squad, and Phil Mafah are running backs who would be available for elevation. Cam Skattebo injury: Giants’ RB a question mark heading into game vs. Eagles - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Cam Skattebo injury: Giants’ RB a question mark heading into game vs. Eagles Cam Skattebo | Getty Images Jeremy Brener · SB Nation Tue, November 3, 2026 at 3:47 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads "It's going to be probably day to day up to the game," Harbaugh said. "We're going to just have to see where we're at. I'll probably have more information toward the end of the week. We'll see on both those guys where we're at." Skattebo has had an up-and-down season for the Giants. He scored a touchdown in the team's Week 1 win against the Dallas Cowboys, but struggled to find the end zone in the next four weeks. He also recorded four fumbles in the team's first five games. Skattebo likely will have a big role when the team plays the Philadelphia Eagles this week if he is able to go.

home.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
home.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Washington got a nice win over a struggling Eagles team last weekend on 339 yards, 16 first downs and a shaky 5-of-13 on third-down tries. Defense is where the team really excelled in that one though, as that unit held Philly to just 5-of-15 on third downs and 268 total yards along with two takeaways. Washington is generally scoring pretty well this year with 20 or more points in five of seven games. Their only defeat to come by more than one score was a 37-20 loss at Dallas in Week 2. The Commanders will be competitive against most teams if they play to their capabilities. As for the Rams, they held the Chargers to just 14 first downs and 6-of-15 on third downs alongside two takeaways. Los Angeles’ offense put up a tepid 281 yards, 16 first downs and 3-of-11 on third-down tries but they didn’t need to be super flashy amid a strong defensive effort. The Rams have scored a combined 59 points over their last two games and they’re feeling confident going into another winnable matchup. It should be a close one. Game Info, Stats and Previews The Los Angeles Rams and the Washington Commanders meet Sunday in NFL action from Northwest Stadium in Summerfield. Here’s a collection of relevant information and reasoning for a sound Commanders vs Rams prediction. We have looked at this information from a betting perspective and attempted to determine the best Commanders vs Rams pick. Los Angeles Rams Betting Preview This year the Rams have been a mixed bag with more downs than ups. Los Angeles started out on a 2-2 run with wins over the New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles mixed with losses to the 49ers and Broncos. After two more losses to the Buffalo Bills and Arizona Cardinals, the Rams posted a win over the Raiders. That victory would bring LA’s record to 3-4 overall through the first seven games. In Sunday’s game versus the Chargers, the Rams gave up a couple of field goals in the second quarter but still had a very small lead 10-9 going into the break. LA came back out with a couple of third-quarter touchdowns and finished off the game with a 24-9 victory. QB Matthew Stafford was 17-of-25 for 157 yards, one TD and one pick. Blake Corum led the rush with 11 totes for 73 yards and a score while Puka Nacua had 11 catches for 80 yards and a touchdown. Washington Commanders Betting Preview Over on the Commanders’ side, they’ve had been worse luck in the win column this year. Washington was only able to win one of their first four games, taking out Seattle on September 27. The losses otherwise were versus Philadelphia, Dallas and Indianapolis. After a tie versus the rival New York Giants, the Commanders took another loss versus the 49ers for a 1-4-1 run through the first six. In the matchup versus Philadelphia, the Commanders gave up a TD and a field goal in the first quarter but then got it going themselves in the second. Washington scored three times for a 13-10 edge at halftime. From there the Commanders held the Eagles scoreless and waltzed into a 27-10 victory. QB Jayden Daniels was 16-of-29 for 217 yards and a TD. Rachaad White had 11 carries for 55 yards and a TD while Treylon Burks had three catches for 81 yards. away.headline: Rams Hit With Concerning Injury News Before Facing Chargers
away.blurb: After the offseason trade to acquire superstar pass rusher Myles Garrett and the move to bring Aaron Donald out of retirement, many were picking the Rams to win it all. Through seven games, the team is just 3-4 and injuries have completely derailed the start of the year. Adam Grosbard of the LA Dailey News shared some rough updates for the Rams. Coleman Shelton, Colby Parkinson, and Trent McDuffie are all questionable to play this week. Joe Cardona is also doubtful to play. At this point in time, no one knows exactly when Garrett will return. There was hope that the Rams could open up his practice window this week, but that didn't end up being the case . The current hope is that Adams could return in the shorter window of the original 6-to-8 week estimate. Rams Hit With Concerning Injury News Before Facing Chargers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL What MLB's labor proposal means Rams Hit With Concerning Injury News Before Facing Chargers (David Brytus-Imagn Images) Evan Massey · Roundtable Sports Sat, October 31, 2026 at 5:58 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams have had a rough all-around start to the 2026 NFL season. Garrett has not played since Week 1. Davante Adams recently went down with a severe hamstring injury and is going to miss a decent amount of time. Puka Nacua is even dealing with a calf injury, although he is trying to play through it. With that being said, more concerning injury news was shared for Los Angeles before this week's game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Missing McDuffie and Parkinson would be a tough blow. However, the loss of Shelton could be the biggest blow of them all. Matthew Stafford has struggled a bit to begin the season. Playing without Shelton would force the Los Angeles offense to play without the anchor of its offensive line. Needless to say, every game at this point is big for the Rams. A 3-4 record isn't too bad by itself, but too many more losses would make recovering late in the year more difficult. Sean McVay and his team simply need to scrape together some wins to stay afloat until players start returning from injury. Going up against the Chargers should give L.A. a good chance to pick up another win. Jim Harbaugh and his team are 0-6 and not many positive signs of improvement have been seen. Hopefully, some of these updates receive good news before Sunday afternoon's game. Kickoff this week against the Chargers is scheduled for 4:05 p.m. ET. Fans will be able to tune in and watch the game on Fox.

home.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay provides key Myles Garrett injury update before Commanders clash
home.blurb: Rams news: Sean McVay provides Myles Garrett injury update before Commanders clash NBA Eastern Atlantic Boston Celtics MLB National East Atlanta Braves NHL Eastern Metropolitan Carolina Hurricanes Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay provided a key injury update for star edge rusher Myles Garrett ahead of the team's upcoming game. Add ClutchPoints on Google Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Currently 4-4 and third in the NFC West, the 2026 campaign has not gone according to plan for the Los Angeles Rams. However, two straight wins have put the Rams right back in the thick of the playoff race. With two road games coming up against the Washington Commanders and Arizona Cardinals, Los Angeles received some promising news. ESPN insider Adam Schefter shared Rams head coach Sean McVay's updates on star edge rusher Myles Garrett and tight end Terrance Ferguson via X, formerly Twitter. “Help is on the way: Myles Garrett will practice this week, and Terrance Ferguson might,” Schefter reposted Monday evening. Acquired this offseason, Garrett was supposed to team up with the returning Aaron Donald to cause havoc in the backfields of the Rams' opponents. However, after a quiet debut in the Rams' Week 1 loss to division rival San Francisco in Australia, Garrett hit the IR. The fact that he'll be able to get back on the field for practice is a massive boost for Los Angeles. If Garrett gets back to the form that helped him break the NFL single season sack record last fall, then he will be a massive headache for the upcoming teams on LA's schedule. Getting Ferguson back should help the offense as well. The unit has been inconsistent at times, but it has improved in the last two wins. With star receiver Davante Adams on the shelf, and Puka Nacua routinely battling some ailment, having Ferguson team up with veteran Tyler Higbee will only help signal caller Matthew Stafford. With wins over the Commanders and the Cardinals over the next two weeks, the Rams could truly be back in contention. Getting both Garrett and Ferguson back on the field should only help Los Angeles going forward. Jordan Llanes is a sports writer and reporter based in Florida. home.blurb: WR Matthew Golden (foot/shoulder): He returned in a limited capacity during Wednesday's walkthrough, keeping the door open to playing Thursday night. Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Cut he gut it out on a short week? The Packers will be thin at defensive tackle once again if Wyatt can't go. He needs to get healthy and start disrupting more plays. home.headline: Panthers' concerns going into Thursday's game against the Packers just got even worse based on the final Week 8 injury report
home.blurb: The Carolina Panthers had a lot of concerns going into this week after the beatdown the team suffered on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. To make things even harder, the Panthers had a short turnaround to make adjustments with a road trip coming up on Thursday against the Green Bay Packers. That already was going to be a rough road matchup for this team with everything going on coming out of the last game, and to make things even worse, the team's final Week 8 injury report added even more concerns. First off, the Panthers have officially ruled out star pass rusher Jaelan Phillips for the second consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Given the nature of the injury, the fact it's a reaggravation, and this being a short week, it was always unlikely that Phillips would have been able to play against the Packers. Wednesday's injury report confirmed those suspicions, leaving the Panthers without their top edge rusher. Being without Phillips really hurt the Panthers last week. Tampa Bay exposed the Panthers in the run game attacking the edges with counters and rumbled for over 250 yards on the ground. It was an embarrassing performance and not having Phillips out there to set the edge was a big reason for it, along with poor tackling. Big picture, sitting Phillips is the right call for him. He needs to get that hamstring figured out before rushing back into action like he did in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which is what caused this injury to reaggravate in the first place. The Panthers need Phillips for the long haul and need him fully healthy before returning. Another notable injury designation is left guard Damien Lewis, who will be out for Thursday's game due to a knee injury. Lewis was easily the team's best offensive lineman, allowing seven pressures this season on over 200 pass blocking snaps. The other four starters have each allowed 15+ pressures this season. The Panthers are also without backup guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and elevated Jake Curhan from the practice squad as a result. The Panthers also placed veteran right tackle Taylor Moton on the injured reserve earlier this week after he fractured his fibula along with further damage to his ankle. That leaves Monroe Freeling to fill back in at right tackle, which in turn forces Rasheed Walker to remain at left tackle. Those two have allowed a combined five sacks and 42 pressures. In Lewis place at left guard, the Panthers will likely turn to Corey Bullock, who's played 71 pass blocking snaps this season with one sack and five pressures allowed. It's a tough look for quarterback Bryce Young, who has been having to overcome pressure all season long. One more worrisome injury to note is in the secondary. Akayleb Evans will not play either due to a triceps/knee injury. Evans has been filling in as a starter, and largely has struggled, in place of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. CBS has the broadcast, and the Texans are favored by 4.5 points, with the total sitting at 40.5. That’s a pretty low number, but take one look at the Chargers’ offense and you’ll understand it. Los Angeles still hasn’t won a game, and Houston hasn’t exactly been lighting up the scoreboard, either. This might not be the prettiest game on Sunday’s schedule. Check out our free NFL picks for more predictions. Houston Texans Need to Take Advantage of This Matchup Houston is 2-5 and coming off its bye week. The Texans lost 27-21 to the Giants in overtime before the break, which was a pretty disappointing result considering they were favored by 10 points. Houston had finally started to turn things around with consecutive victories, then went right back to making mistakes against a team it should have beaten. That’s what bothers me about the Texans. They’ve got enough talent to be better than 2-5, but they haven’t been consistent enough to trust. The offense can move the ball, but finishing drives has been a problem. Against the Chargers, Houston doesn’t need to get into a scoring contest. It needs to avoid turnovers, establish the run, and make Los Angeles prove it can score. The extra week of preparation should help. Houston has had time to work on some of the problems that showed up against New York, and now it gets a Chargers team that’s struggling badly. But I’d still like to see the Texans put together a complete game before giving them too much credit. They’ve been favored before and found ways to lose. Los Angeles Chargers Are Running Out of Answers The Chargers are 0-7 after losing 24-9 to the Rams on Sunday. Nine points, all on field goals. That’s a pretty rough afternoon, especially when you’re playing in your own stadium. Los Angeles was only down 10-9 at halftime, so the game was there for the taking. Then the Chargers went scoreless in the second half. And that’s the problem with this team. The defense can keep things respectable for a while, but the offense hasn’t been doing enough to win. Los Angeles also lost 22-6 to Kansas City in Week 6. That’s 15 points over those two games, and you’re not beating many NFL teams with that kind of production. I will say this for the Chargers. They’re at home, and Houston hasn’t been particularly impressive. If Los Angeles can get its running game going and avoid putting everything on the passing attack, it might be able to hang around. But the Chargers have to start finishing drives. Settling for field goals is one thing. Going an entire half without scoring is another. I know the Texans are 2-5, and that’s not exactly the kind of record that makes you want to rush to the betting window. But the Chargers are winless, and their offense has been miserable. Los Angeles scored nine points against the Rams and six against Kansas City. Houston doesn’t need to be spectacular to cover this number. It just needs to get into the low 20s and make the Chargers chase the game. The bye week helps, too. Give me the Texans to win by at least a touchdown. Total Pick: Under 40.5 Give me the under 40.5. Normally, I’d be a little nervous taking an under this low, but I keep coming back to the Chargers’ offense. Fifteen points over their last two games against the Rams and Chiefs isn’t much to work with. Houston has also had trouble finishing drives, so I don’t expect the Texans to put up 35. This looks like a game where both teams spend plenty of time trying to establish the run and avoid mistakes. The danger is a defensive touchdown or a couple of short fields. Otherwise, I can see something like 23-13, and that stays under. Safety Derwin James Jr., who's missed the Chargers' last three games with a nagging hamstring injury, now may be headed to injured reserve, head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters on Wednesday. What's wrong with Derwin James? As detailed by Elliott Teaford of the Orange County Register , the move to place James on IR isn't official yet, but Harbaugh said "it's looking like he may go to IR." Jun 17, 2026; El Segundo, CA, USA; Los Angeles Chargers safety Derwin James (3) during minicamp at The Bolt. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) He'd miss games against the LA Rams, Houston Texans, Baltimore Ravens and New York Jets, but could come back to play against the New England Patriots. It's a devastating blow for a team in desperate need of a spark, particularly given the expectations placed upon James this offseason. The Chargers rewarded James' elite play with a huge contract extension that made him the highest paid safety in the NFL for the second time in his career. Between James' injury and a struggling offense, though, the Chargers are now the last winless team in the NFL. What does Derwin James mean to the Chargers? So far this season, James' stats haven't exactly jumped off the page. In his three games, he had 21 tackles and broke up a pass. Those numbers, though, belie a spectacular resume thus far. In the six seasons in which he's played at least 14 games, he's been a Pro Bowler five times and an All Pro four times. That kind of production and experience is impossible to replace, and this Sunday, Matthew Stafford and the Rams might have a field day with the Bolts defense. Considering the Rams are also looking to rebound from a poor start to the year, this battle for LA supremacy might be the defining week for both franchises. home.blurb: Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have been ruled out for Sunday's game at Miami. Brown and Henderson were among those listed as questionable on the team's injury report Friday. Brown hurt his knee during Wednesday's practice, after which he was listed with knee and ankle injuries for the first time this season. He did not practice Thursday or Friday. At running back, Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner are expected to take most, if not all, of the carries, while Larison contributes primarily on special teams. On Friday, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel expressed optimism the team could replace any players who might be out in Miami. On Saturday, the Patriots also ruled out backup offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who has been designated to return off injured reserve but not activated to the 53-man roster. Cornerback Carlton Davis (neck) and linebacker Christian Elliss (chest) are still listed as questionable for kickoff, though Davis has indicated he expects to play for the first time in three weeks. home.blurb: As the result of extended time from last Thursday's loss to Chicago, positive light has been shined on an injury riddled Patriots team — which is RotoWire's eighth-highest ranked team when it comes to injury impacts. On the first injury report of Week 8, the Patriots have their least amount of limited or non-participants since Week 1's opening practice. Three immediate pieces that standout on the injury report is the return of cornerbacks Carlton Davis, Channing Canada, and Karon Prunty. The three have each missed four games this season, leaving the cornerback room to rely on star Christian Gonzalez — who's also faced injury troubles this season — Marcus Jones, and Charles Woods. "I'm happy to be back out here and be a full go," said Davis ahead of Wednesday's practice. The Patriots offensive line drills had Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse starting. After sustaining the injury against the Jets, Moses activation against Chicago came as somewhat of a surprise, as the 35-year-old was able to play the entire game. Still listed as limited six days later, his status will be one to watch in the coming days. Another thing to note is Marcus Bryant's full participation on Wednesday. He's been out since the start of the season and is still on the injured reserve, though his IR activiation period is coming to a close soon — meaning the Patriots will have to decide whether they use one of their five remaining injured reserve activations for the season on Bryant. Brown is listed with an ankle injury and was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. His ankle injury is the same one he suffered in Week 1 against Seattle that landed him on injured reserve. picks.blurb: Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Raiders vs. 49ers bold predictions for NFL Week 9 Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:56 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Las Vegas Raiders arrive at Levi's Stadium with renewed confidence. The San Francisco 49ers arrive with extra rest and something to prove. Las Vegas snapped a four-game losing streak with a 38–33 victory over the Jets, improving to 4–4. San Francisco, meanwhile, returns from its bye at 6–1 after suffering its first defeat, a 29–20 loss to Atlanta. Their November 8 matchup offers a test of whether the Raiders' rebound represents progress or another temporary escape. The opening market favors San Francisco by 10 points, with a total of 51.5. These predictions envision something more explosive than that total suggests: a quarterback showcase, a monster receiving performance and a decisive fourth-quarter separation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brock Purdy throws for 350 yards and four touchdowns Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Purdy will deliver his most convincing statistical statement of the season, reaching 350 passing yards and throwing four touchdown passes. That projection starts with a favorable matchup. Las Vegas has surrendered at least 30 points in five consecutive games, allowing opponents to dictate too many possessions. Even Sunday's victory required the Raiders to overcome 33 points from the Jets. Purdy already has 1,748 passing yards and 15 touchdowns through seven games. Before the bye, he threw for 288 yards against Atlanta despite injuries affecting several important offensive contributors. The Raiders should expect Kyle Shanahan to test their coverage communication immediately. Motion, play-action and layered routes can create uncertainty without requiring Purdy to hold the ball for extended periods. My projection anticipates San Francisco attacking through the air even after establishing a lead. Rather than leaning exclusively on clock management, Shanahan will keep exploiting favorable matchups. Brock Bowers produces 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns The Raiders' best answer will come through Brock Bowers, who will turn a difficult road assignment into a dominant individual performance. The prediction is at least 150 receiving yards and two touchdowns, including one reception covering 40 or more yards. That would require Las Vegas to build its passing plan around Bowers rather than waiting for him to emerge naturally within the progression. Quick throws would establish his involvement, while crossing routes and seam opportunities would provide the bigger gains. Kirk Cousins enters the matchup following a three-touchdown performance against the Jets, and his recent play has kept rookie Fernando Mendoza on the sideline. That continuity matters for this prediction. The Raiders can attack with an experienced quarterback rather than simplifying everything around a developmental transition. The projected game script should also create volume. If San Francisco scores early, Las Vegas will need to maintain an aggressive passing approach rather than protect field position. Bowers would become the central answer, particularly on third downs and near the goal line. His production will keep the Raiders competitive longer than expected, even as their defense struggles to match it. The teams combine for 70 points as San Francisco wins 42–28 The final prediction is a shootout that eventually becomes a comfortable 49ers victory. A 42–28 result would produce 70 total points, sailing past the opening 51.5-point total while giving San Francisco a 14-point winning margin. The logic connects the first two bold predictions, Purdy repeatedly punishes defensive breakdowns, while Cousins and Bowers generate enough offense to prevent an early rout. Ultimately, the difference will be possession-to-possession consistency. Las Vegas will manufacture explosive moments, but San Francisco will sustain more scoring drives and turn one late Raiders mistake into the decisive touchdown. The Raiders will show offensive resilience. The 49ers will show why their ceiling remains substantially higher. Guard Jackson Powers-Johnson (back) was a non-participant in Thursday’s practice but was upgraded to limited on Friday and listed as questionable for Sunday. Bailey didn’t practice at all during the week. Additionally, running back Breece Hall (quad) and offensive lineman/former Raider Dylan Parham (knee) are questionable. San Francisco 49ers get unexpected good news on injured rookie star as De'Zhaun Stribling makes major progress in recovery
home.blurb: The 49ers have been waiting for encouraging news about their injured rookie receiver, and the latest development offers fresh hope for a late-season return. Stribling suffered a Grade 3 left ankle deltoid ligament sprain during San Francisco's Week 1 game against the Los Angeles Rams, a game the 49ers dominated . The rookie underwent surgery in mid-September and landed on injured reserve with the expectation that he would miss multiple months. There is a chance he is on track to return in December. Christian Kirk has already returned from injury and is looking to increase his snap count. Mike Evans has been dealing with a rib injury along with Achilles soreness . Even so, Evans looks to be on track to keep playing. Deebo Samuel also appears to be recovering well from his hamstring injury and looks close to a return. Does the fact that he can walk again guarantee a December return? No. Recovery from an injury like this rarely moves in a straight line. Still, I'll take a rookie walking around the locker room without crutches or a brace less than two months after surgery every single time. picks.headline: Cardinals vs Seahawks Prediction & Tips: Week 9
Seahawks vs. Cardinals odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Cardinals odds: Opening lines for Week 9 matchup | Field Gulls Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Seattle Seahawks Community Field Gulls November 4, 2026 Field Gulls Notifications Notifications Sections Pre-Snap Reads By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds Seattle Seahawks Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Sections Expand Pre-Snap Reads By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Seattle Seahawks Odds The Seahawks enter as double-digit favorites despite another frustrating defeat on Monday. While there isn’t much positivity about the Seattle Seahawks from fans following the team’s blowout loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday, that hasn’t slowed confidence from oddsmakers ahead of their Week 9 game. According to the current odds on FanDuel Sportsbook , the Seahawks enter their second game against the Arizona Cardinals as 10.5-point favorites (-110) , with Seattle’s moneyline is set at -650 , while Arizona’s sits at +480 . The over/under line for the game is 44.5 , indicating that the Seahawks, now 4-4, are more than likely headed for another defensive slogfest against the Cardinals. The man trusted to score those points for the Cardinals will be none other than Washington State alum Gardner Minshew, who brought his patented good vibes to Arizona in the team’s second-half upset of the Dallas Cowboys in Week 8. Minshew ignited a spark in the Cardinals’ offense, which helped them score the most points, 33, that they’ve scored in a game all year. Arizona’s gutsy win in overtime against the Dallas Cowboys lifted them to 3-5 on the season. Aside from Minshew, running back Tyler Allgier had a career day after taking over for rookie Jeremiyah Love. The journeyman quarterback’s favorite target was Michael Wilson, who willed his team to a win with two broken ribs. The health of Wilson may be paramount to the Cardinals’ offense as he offers a second option for Minshew when superstar tight end Trey McBride is covered. While the Cardinals beat up on a reeling Cowboys’ defense, a trip to Seattle to play Mike Macdonald’s unit is an entirely different story. This unit held the Cardinals to 7 points in Week 2 and stifled much of Arizona’s run game. However, the story of these two teams’ early meeting was the Seahawks’ offense, which totaled 24 points in the second half after a slow start. Seattle, which was led by Drew Lock at the time, was led by their offensive engine, Jaxon Smith-Njigba. JSN totaled three touchdowns and 155 yards in that game, a performance the struggling Seahawks would love to see again. Unlike most of their games in 2026, the Seahawks had success on the ground in Week 2 with Emmanuel Wilson running for 92 yards and rookie Jadarian Price adding 52 yards. Guard-Imagn Images It is quite easy to blame the Seattle Seahawks ' uneven first half on an inefficient run game, but the defending Super Bowl champions did not exactly post eye-popping numbers on the ground during the 2025 regular season. They averaged 4.1 yards per carry and ranked 11th in the league with 123.3 rushing yards per week. Though, even when the backfield was lacking firepower, it still posed a threat to defenses. The 2026 Seahawks are hoping to get that back on Monday. Emanuel Wilson has done his best to shoulder the burden following Kenneth Walker III's free-agency departure and multiple injuries to the position group, eclipsing 80 rushing yards on three separate occasions. He can use some help, though. An incoming future Hall of Fame offensive lineman like Quenton Nelson should provide a huge boost , but a versatile RB room is an important element of many successful teams. And Seattle (4-3) is ready to shake things up a bit. Zach Charbonnet is expected to make his season debut versus the Chicago Bears , and although he is still on injured reserve at time of print, rookie Jadarian Price is in line to join him. The former is returning from a torn ACL he suffered in the playoffs back in January, and the latter logged full practice participation on Friday after missing the last month of action with a chest injury. The Bears are inserting All-Pro defensive tackle and big midseason acquisition Jeffery Simmons into their front seven, so the Seahawks may have a better chance of keeping Chicago on its toes with their top-three ball-carriers. Fans have seen what quarterback Sam Darnold can accomplish when Seattle establishes its ground attack. Even without Kyle Monangai, who is still battling turf toe and a thumb injury, the Bears boast a dangerous D'Andre Swift-led rushing unit. The Seahawks must close the gap in that crucial area on Monday night. Their chances of doing so have seemingly improved. Opening kickoff will commence at 8:15 p.m. ET. Tampa Bay just beat Atlanta 16–0 without completing a pass. Chicago comes in off an upset of Seattle. The Bears are 6-point favorites, and the total is 46.5. The Bucs have won three of their last four after an 0–4 start, so they are still in the NFC South race. These predictions lean on the contrast between Tampa Bay's run-first plan and Chicago's explosive offense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Caleb Williams leads the Bears past 30 points again Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images Chicago will score at least 30 points, and Williams will account for three touchdowns. The Bears have scored 30 or more in every game Williams has finished this season, and they have not lost one he has started and finished (4–0). Since he returned from his hamstring injury, they have not trailed in any of three games. Williams threw for 308 yards and two touchdowns in a 30–24 win over New England. Chicago's pass offense averages 236.4 yards a game compared with 131.4 for Tampa Bay. That edge in the air is the core of this call. Tampa Bay's pass defense gives up 205.9 yards a game, which leaves room for chunk plays. Chicago's offense ranks 10th in EPA per play despite Williams missing three full games. I expect him to throw for at least 275 yards and add a rushing score. The one wrinkle is the Bears' backfield. Running back Kyle Monangai is listed as out with a thumb injury, which could shift more of the offense to Williams. Tampa Bay runs for 200 yards and still loses The Bucs will pile up another 200 rushing yards, and it still won't be enough. Against Atlanta, Tampa Bay ran 56 times for 324 yards. Bucky Irving gained 170 yards on 27 carries, and Kenny Gainwell added 140 on 25. Baker Mayfield attempted only three passes in steady rain. Chicago's run defense is beatable, allowing 4.4 yards per carry. Tampa Bay ranks eighth in EPA per rush, so the ground game will work on Sunday night. The problem is what happens when Chicago scores early. The Bucs average 22.3 points a game. A team rated poorly through the air can't easily come back against the best third-down defense in football, according to one projection. I'm projecting 200 rushing yards because the Bears' run defense can't stop everything. But Tampa Bay's offense needs scoring drives, not just yards, and the run game alone won't produce 30 points. Injuries make it harder. Gainwell is questionable with a hip issue, and outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was trending toward out. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka was inactive last week with a foot injury and is also a concern. Mayfield throws 35 passes and the Bears win 34–20 The game ends with Chicago winning 34–20, and Mayfield forced into a very different afternoon than the one in Tampa. A 34–20 final would add up to 54 points, clearing the 46.5 total comfortably, and it would give Chicago a 14-point cover. Mayfield returned from a fractured thumb two games ago and is still working back to full rhythm. He has 679 passing yards and three touchdowns on the season, so asking him to throw 35 times is a real shift for this offense. That volume creates risk. If Chicago leads by two scores in the third quarter, Tampa Bay has to abandon the run and put the ball in Mayfield's hands. I expect two interceptions, including one that sets up a Chicago touchdown. The Bucs will compete. They'll move the ball, their kicker has been perfect this season and their defense will make a few plays. But the Bears' offense is more dangerous, and they are better built to play with a lead. away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). away.headline: Falcons Have Another Lengthy Injury Report vs. Buccaneers, 1 Player Out Already
away.blurb: Falcons Have Another Lengthy Injury Report vs. Buccaneers, 1 Player Out Already Skip to main content SI.COM The Falcons officially ruled out running back Brian Robinson Jr. on Friday due to a hamstring injury, marking his second consecutive absence. Khalil Herbert will be his likely replacement after a good showing last week in a win over the 49ers. Robinson has not been able to return to the field since suffering the injury, leaving Atlanta without one of its primary options behind Bijan Robinson. While Robinson is the only player officially ruled out, the Falcons have several other injury concerns heading into Sunday’s divisional matchup. Eight players are listed as questionable, including three defensive players who could have significant roles against Tampa Bay. Defensive backs Billy Bowman Jr. and Avieon Terrell are both questionable. Bowman is dealing with a hamstring injury, while Terrell has been working through an illness. Both players missed Atlanta’s victory over San Francisco last week. Linebacker Divine Deablo is also questionable with a forearm injury. His potential absence would be notable for Atlanta’s defense, as Deablo has served as one of the unit’s primary communicators this season. The remaining questionable players include wide receivers Beaux Collins (hip) and Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder), defensive ends Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and Charles Snowden (back), and offensive tackle Cameron Williams (ankle). There is some encouraging news for Atlanta heading into the weekend. Collins and Williams both participated fully in Friday’s practice, while the other questionable players were limited participants. The Falcons have no players listed as doubtful. Falcons Rule Out Two Key Defensive Starters Ahead of Buccaneers Showdown The Atlanta Falcons will be without another key offensive player when they travel to Tampa to face the Buccaneers in Week 8. Bijan Robinson is expected to continue leading the rushing attack, but losing another running back limits Atlanta’s depth at the position. Rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels stepped into a larger role against the 49ers and delivered one of the biggest performances of his young career. Daniels helped seal the victory with a late interception of Brock Purdy. Atlanta will need as many healthy players as possible against a Tampa Bay team coming off a convincing 43-13 victory over the Carolina Panthers. The Buccaneers enter Sunday’s matchup looking to build on that performance, while the Falcons are coming off a 29-20 victory over the previously undefeated 49ers. Atlanta and Tampa Bay will meet Sunday, Nov. 1, at Raymond James Stadium. Kickoff is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. away.blurb: There was some encouraging news for Tampa Bay, as outside linebacker Yaya Diaby (illness) and linebacker Josiah Trotter (illness) were both upgraded to full participation after being limited and sidelined, respectively, during Wednesday's practice. Wide receivers Chris Godwin Jr. and running back Bucky Irving did not practice due to scheduled rest, while defensive lineman A'Shawn Robinson was limited for the same reason. Meanwhile, Atlanta saw several players return to practice Thursday. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) were both upgraded to limited participation after missing Wednesday's session. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith also returned in a limited capacity after receiving a rest day Wednesday. Atlanta continued to have several players limited, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). away.headline: Atlanta Falcons @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers: Who's On The Injury Report?
away.blurb: Backup running back Brian Robinson Jr. had already missed Week Seven against the San Francisco 49ers with a hamstring injury. That injury lingers, and he is out this week. Khalil Herbert will continue to back up starting running back Bijan Robinson in the backfield. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. was downgraded to out with a hamstring injury. With veteran safety Jessie Bates III , veteran defensive back Sydney Brown, and young safety Xavier Watts making the middle of the field a tough place to play for opposing offenses, Bowman Jr. has enough reinforcements to heal. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out again with a foot injury. Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. have been a one-two punch for Tampa this year, with almost identical stats. The main difference is that Egbuka has the touchdowns, with two this season. We will see how much that affects Tampa's offense on Sunday. Backup running back Kenny Gainwell and offensive tackle Luke Goedeke are both questionable and could also miss Sunday's game, hindering the offense. Last week's game plan was to lean on the run game, which will be harder without the backup running back and with an offensive lineman out. On paper, the Falcons have the advantage heading into Sunday's game. But you never know how these things play out. It bodes well for the Falcons to take advantage and win on Sunday, as it would give them control of the NFC South. picks.blurb: Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football First CFP rankings NFL execs talk trades What MLB's labor proposal means Week 9 Waiver Wire NFL Power Rankings Bills vs. Vikings bold predictions for Week 9 Monday Night Football Garrett Kerman, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 3, 2026 at 5:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Two 6-1 teams enter Monday Night Football with very different questions. Can the Buffalo Bills keep rolling against the NFL's stingiest defense? Can the Minnesota Vikings generate enough offense to avoid wasting another strong defensive performance? Buffalo visits U.S. Bank Stadium on November 9 following a 36–10 victory over Baltimore. Minnesota returns home after Detroit ended its unbeaten start with a 19–15 win. The Bills opened as three-point favorites, setting up a compelling clash between offensive firepower and defensive disruption. These three predictions anticipate a departure from Minnesota's usual defensive script, explosive passing, costly mistakes and a dramatic finish that hands Buffalo its second defeat. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Justin Jefferson explodes for 175 yards and two touchdowns Matt Krohn-Imagn Images Jefferson will deliver the performance Minnesota has been waiting for, finishing with at least 175 receiving yards and two touchdowns. Jefferson caught five passes for 33 yards and a touchdown against Detroit and enters Week 9 without a 100-yard receiving game. Buffalo presents an opportunity to change that. Its defense ranks 30th against the pass, making this a matchup Minnesota should attack rather than approach conservatively. The Vikings need to manufacture touches before asking Jefferson to win difficult downfield assignments. Motion, condensed formations and crossing routes would help create cleaner releases and give the quarterback defined throwing windows. The bigger gains should follow when Buffalo adjusts to those shorter completions. One double move or broken coverage could turn a productive evening into a spectacular one. Quarterback availability remains important. Kyler Murray is managing hamstring tightness , with Carson Wentz the likely alternative if Murray cannot play. Expect Minnesota to make its best receiver the centerpiece, not merely a name opponents must account for. Josh Allen accounts for four touchdowns but commits three turnovers Allen will produce enough spectacular plays to keep Buffalo dangerous and enough mistakes to give Minnesota control of the outcome. The bold prediction is four total touchdowns alongside three turnovers, including at least two interceptions. https://twitter.com/search?q=josh%20allen&src=typed_query&f=top Minnesota's defense provides the foundation for that aggressive forecast. Entering Week 9, the Vikings lead the league in points allowed per game at 13.3, quarterback pressure rate at 45.8 percent and sack percentage at 10.96 percent. Pressure alone will not neutralize Allen. His ability to escape the pocket can turn a successful blitz into a defensive emergency, particularly when coverage players must chase receivers across the field. That creates the central tension. Minnesota will win several snaps decisively, but Allen will punish a few failed pressure attempts with explosive completions or scrambling opportunities. The turnovers will come when he tries to rescue plays that should end with a throwaway. Disguised coverage behind an apparent blitz can invite exactly that kind of aggressive decision. Buffalo's offensive line also bears watching. Right tackle Spencer Brown's availability is a concern entering the matchup, potentially complicating protection against Minnesota's pressure packages. Allen will remain the game's most dangerous improviser. On this night, improvisation will carry a substantial price. Minnesota wins 38–35 on a last-second field goal The final bold prediction ties those individual performances together: Minnesota wins a shootout with a field goal as time expires. A 38–35 result would produce 73 points, comfortably exceeding the opening total of 46.5. It would also represent a dramatic departure from the Vikings' defensive scoring average. The logic is not that Minnesota suddenly becomes a bad defense. Turnovers and explosive plays can produce points without requiring long, methodical drives. Jefferson's breakout keeps the Vikings moving, while Allen repeatedly answers before one late mistake gives Minnesota the deciding possession. After losing its unbeaten record, Minnesota will respond with its most convincing offensive statement and a victory that reinforces its place among the league's contenders. Of course, that could also happen before we get to Thursday or Sunday as well, with general managers working the phones tirelessly this time of year. But it feels quite important when we're talking about matchups like Bills-Vikings or Buccaneers-Bears or Packers-Patriots or even Raiders-49ers on the Week 9 docket. But regardless of what trades transpire, we press forward with our NFL picks this season. It was a decent enough showing for our predictions last week, but we need to make up ground. Toughest NFL Week 9 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills (-3) vs. Minnesota Vikings Buffalo Bills (-3) vs. Minnesota Vikings The NFL saved the best for last in Week 9 with this showdown on Monday night. It's not a dissimilar matchup to what we just saw for the Vikings last week. Brian Flores' all-world defense will be matched up with the best offense in the NFL behind Josh Allen. And though Minnesota lost for the first time this past week, the defense did its job, shutting down the Lions' potent attack and allowing only 19 points in the game. Yet, we're riding with the Bills on Monday night. A sizable part of the reasoning behind that starts with the fact that the Bills offense is just better and more dangerous. Allen is playing out of his mind right now and that group appears to be getting healthier. But more importantly, Buffalo's weakness, much like Detroit, is the defense. With Kyler Murray, though, the Vikings don't have an offense that can take advantage of that. Minnesota simply isn't going to be able to keep up in this one, even if they slow down Allen and the Bills. Even on the road, Buffalo gets it done — and by more than a field goal Easiest NFL Week 9 pick on the board San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Las Vegas Raiders vs. San Francisco 49ers (-9.5) Las Vegas Raiders vs. San Francisco 49ers (-9.5) If the Las Vegas Raiders have proen one thing to us this season, it's the notion that they are this year's "good-bad" team. You know, the team that can get wins against the dregs of the league and look good doing it, but when they're matched up against legitimate playoff contenders, they simply can't stack up. So yeah, that presents a little bit of a problem for the Silver and Black on Sunday as they travel to San Francisco to take on the 49ers. Even with the myriad of injuries that has left the Niners shorthanded for much of the season, they're still rolling at 6-1 and, perhaps more importantly, had some time to recooperate on the bye last week. Their defense is going to slow down Vegas' offense, which is the clear strength of the Raiders, but I don't think the Raiders defense is going to have a single answer for Brock Purdy and Co. Kyle Shanahan is going to make this game look like it's played on easy mode, which should lead to a decisive and one-sided home victory for San Francisco. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott, wide receiver George Pickens | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (-5.5) vs. Indianapolis Colts Dallas Cowboys (-5.5) vs. Indianapolis Colts Naturally, the Cowboys were the easiest pick on the board last week and things went swimmingly... oh, you mean they coughed up a two-score lead in the fourth quarter to Gardner Minshew? Well, that's not good. You probably shouldn't take Dallas going on the road against Indianapolis in Week 9 then. First off, let me make my mistakes. More importantly, though, the Cowboys are the epitome of a Jekyll and Hyde team this season. They can't string together wins, but they have shown the ability to beat up bad teams. Arizona could qualify there, but the Cardinals have shown signs of life throughout the season. I don't know if that's been true about the Colts for a month or more, however. They're preparing for a fire sale — and have already sold off two massive pieces — which means they're likely shorthanded and unmotivated in this game. Dallas isn't a team that anyone should trust on a regular basis. They're the bane of every fan's existence, having to watch this team for three hours every Sunday. But this isn't picking the Cowboys as much as it is an all-out fade of the Colts. This team looks like the most hapless in the league, and there's no way anyone can get behind them with a shred of confidence right now. home.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions' injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday's game, which means he's likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he's likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR.
